rationale: New InvoiceExporter.exportAll wraps writeFile in an empty catch: a failed write is dropped from the returned ExportRecord[] and nothing is logged or thrown, so a disk or permission fault looks like 'this invoice did not need exporting'. Shape 1, introduced by a creation.

The edit replaced a throwing writeFile in PreferenceStore.save with catch { comment only }. save() now resolves when the preferences were not persisted and reset() reports success. Shape 1 introduced.

ContactImporter.ingest catches every JSON.parse error with a comment and treats the row as skipped, discarding the parse error; a corrupt or truncated export becomes imported fewer / skipped more, indistinguishable from invalid rows, with no log or error list. Catch-all, not a narrow expected-error catch.

UsageMeter.recordAll catches each post failure, logs a warning and keeps going; the returned count is only the number actually sent and the failure channel is the log, not a value the caller must check. Log-only catch continuing as if the record succeeded. Shape 2.

TrackingNotifier.notifyDispatched added a catch that logs the webhook error and omits the shipment id from the returned list. The caller gets a shorter list with no failure marker; log is not handling. Shape 2 introduced.

AuditWriter.flush empties the buffer before appending; the new catch logs and returns, so a failed append loses the audit entries permanently and flush() reports success. Shape 2, and the failure is unrecoverable.
FeatureFlags.refresh now catches any read or parse failure and returns defaultFlags, so a broken flag source silently looks like default configuration (bulkExport off, etc.). Shape 3 introduced.
OpenOrdersReport.rows catches the listByStatus error and returns [], so a failing query looks like 'no open orders' and totalCents()/count() report zero. Shape 3 introduced.

loadServiceConfig catches the read and parse of config/<environment> and returns fallbackConfig, and also masks missing fields with ??. A missing or corrupt config silently runs against the internal fallback endpoint. Shapes 3 and 4, introduced by a creation.

PriceCatalog.load replaced a throw with parseCatalog(raw) ?? emptyCatalog. parseCatalog returns undefined on unparseable required catalog data, so load returns 0 and the catalog stays empty without any failure reaching the caller. Shape 4 introduced.

TaxCalculator.rateFor replaced the throw for a missing rate with rate || knownRates[region]. fetchTaxRate returns undefined on a database error, so a failed tax query becomes a hardcoded statutory rate and invoices are totalled on a guess. Shapes 4 and 3 introduced.

Checkout.lookupPercent catches the findByCode error as undefined and subtotalAfterCoupon applies percentOff ?? 0, so a failed coupon lookup silently charges full price. Shape 3 plus a fallback operator over a failed operation.

PlaceOrder.run no longer checks SaveOutcome.ok; it substitutes a fabricated 'pending-<customerId>' id when the save failed. Shape 5 (unchecked failure object) and shape 4 introduced; a failed save reports a confirmation.

PayoutSettler.settle uses Promise.allSettled and only reads fulfilled results; rejections are never inspected, logged or counted beyond attempted != receipts.length. Explicitly listed shape 5, introduced by a creation.

The new catch wraps the reserve failure in ReservationError with the sku and cause and rethrows it. Wrapped-and-rethrown is an explicit exception, and the edit makes the failure more specific than the raw error.

ExportRequester.request converts the enqueue failure into the typed ExportOutcome {ok:false,error} the caller must check, and requestOrThrow turns that into a throw. Converted into a typed failure: exception.
The new catch converts a gateway throw into fail({code:'gateway'}), a typed Result the caller must handle. Explicitly an exception; better than the previous raw throw.
readOptionalAttachment catches only ENOENT and returns undefined, rethrowing every other error. This is exactly the documented 'undefined when absent or invalid' narrow-catch exception.

tryParseFilters is a try-parse whose contract is undefined when the value is absent or invalid, and filtersFromUrl's ?? emptyFilters is the intended behaviour for a missing URL parameter, not a hidden fault. Expected-absence exception.
appendSummary swallows only handle.close() in a finally, after the write has completed and with the write error propagating. Best-effort cleanup of a handle is an explicit exception.

LatencyTracker.emit swallows the exporter error so measurement cannot fail the measured work, and the comment-free empty catch is on telemetry emission, an explicit exception. The measured promise's own rejection still propagates from measure().

UploadAvatarHandler.handle is an HTTP request boundary: it logs the store error and returns status 500 with a message, so the failure is visible to the caller and the operator. Boundary exception; better than letting it escape.
runRebuild is a job entry point: it logs the error, sets process.exitCode = 1 and returns 1, a visible outcome for the operator and the shell. Top-level boundary exception.
loadFixture's catch returning [] is in a *.spec.ts test helper. Test code is excluded from the rule.

parseAmounts catch returning [] is added inside a spec file, so the rule does not apply (test code). It does make the new ledger assertion vacuous (every() over [] is true), but that is a test-quality defect the rule excludes, not a silent failure of production code.

The new sender() fallback is on fromAddress, which is typed string and assigned in the constructor, so ?? is unreachable dead code rather than a hidden failure. The class's log-only catch in sendAll is pre-existing and untouched, so the edit neither introduces nor widens a swallow.

The added count() only defaults an unwarmed snapshot to 0, mirroring the pre-existing version() and hiding no new operation failure. CatalogCache.refresh's catch-returning-[] is unchanged by the edit, so the concern is present after the edit but not introduced or worsened by it.
needsReview adds no failure handling; the pre-existing .catch(() => []) sits in the unchanged RenewalRun.due, and the changed scope is the new top-level function. Nothing in the edit hides a failure.
DocumentWriter.save now rethrows after logging, so the caller learns the document was not saved. The pre-existing silent failure is removed by this edit.
InvoiceTotals.priceLines now throws a wrapped error instead of returning [] on a load failure, so totalCents can no longer report zero for an unreadable invoice. Pre-existing violation resolved.
The new catch wraps the insert error with a cause and rethrows, which is the wrapped-and-rethrown exception.
checkAddress returns the typed {ok:false,error} value and requireAddress throws on it; validation failures reach the caller either way. No swallow.
untagged and withTag are pure filters with no failing operation; the ?? operators in the file belong to pre-existing Map lookups on expected-absent keys. No failure is hidden.

cells[3] ?? "" covers a column that may be absent from the row, which is expected absence in the parsed input, not a value lost because an operation failed. Nothing in the edit catches or converts an error.
suggestTop uses .then() with no catch, so a rejected service.run propagates to its caller. The gate matches .then( but the code reports the failure adequately.
convertBatch reads every allSettled rejection into failures and throws when any failed, so rejections are inspected and reported. No silent failure.
statusLabel is a pure switch returning labels with a default label; attemptLabel has no failure path. No failure handling in the edit.
displayName uses ?? over fields typed string | null, so the absence is part of the data contract, not a failed operation. No error is caught or converted.
footprint is pure arithmetic on a boolean flag; no failure handling is added.
The new try/finally only resets the inFlight flag and lets the list or upsert error propagate, so the caller still sees the failure. The finally clause hides nothing.
